note: Pension portal required field is backed, but the HR consumer (correspondence and payroll administration) is only weakly inferred from the address quote, and the passport/ID help text and trim validation are not backed by any cited fact.
Pension fund required field is backed, but HR consumer (correspondence/payroll), the passport/ID help text and trim validation are not supported by the cited facts.
Required field, DD.MM.YYYY display and ISO storage are backed, but the validation rules (valid calendar date, not in the future) are not supported by any cited fact.
HR needs full postal address including street, and nothing extra, so the required text field is backed.
Required house number for HR is backed, but the free-text allowing '12a' is not stated in the cited facts.
Postcode is required for HR address, and no format check is consistent with G-06 (no source gives one).
Town is part of the complete address HR requires.
Country is part of HR's address, ISO alpha-2 is per G-09, and use as residence country for source tax is backed by F-TR-037/040/043/045.

The 26 labels and required status are backed, but the two-letter option values and the ask_when address_country=="CH" restriction are not backed by the cited facts (F-SC-018 leaves residents abroad and residence-vs-work canton unresolved).
Source-tax liability needs nationality for people living in CH (F-TR-040/041), residents abroad are always subject (F-TR-037), and G-01 backs asking only when needed.
The C-permit exemption (F-TR-025/040/042), the first-day permit reminder (F-TR-029), and the option values (G-10) back the field and its ask condition.
The first working day is needed for the fund, is confirmed by the employee, changes often, and the insurance start is derived from it (F-TR-015/016/019, G-08).
The fund's required dropdown with exactly four options (F-SC-009/010, G-07), the source-tax use (F-TR-031/030), and the values (G-10) are all backed.
Asking when married, required, and the DD.MM.YYYY format are backed, but the 'must not be in the future' validation is not backed by any cited fact.
The spouse-exemption rule (F-TR-031/033/040) and the ask condition limited to cases where the exemption could apply (F-TR-044) are backed.
The spouse's permit matters only for non-Swiss spouses (F-TR-034/035) and only when the exemption could apply (F-TR-044), with option values per G-10.

Facts support asking spouse residence for the exemption, but the country-type ISO alpha-2 format/validation and required_when=true are not backed, and the 'ask_when' narrowing is only inferred, since facts only give 'lives here' (in CH), not a country field.

Calculator asking whether the spouse works for married employees is supported (F-TR-030), but the boolean yes/no format, validation and required_when=true are not backed, and the notes admit the calculator wording is unknown.
F-TR-040, F-TR-025, F-TR-031 and F-TR-037 back every branch: abroad always subject, and in CH exempt if Swiss, C permit, or married to a Swiss/C-permit spouse living in CH.
F-TR-017/018/019 give the derivation rule and F-SC-007/008 give the pension fund's required DD.MM.YYYY 1st-of-month format.
F-TR-013 confirms the photo is postponed to next year because of the badge system change.
F-TR-028 and G-03 confirm IT equipment is out of scope because IT has its own process.
G-03 explicitly puts AHV data out of scope.
F-TR-019 and G-08 state the insurance start date is derived from first_working_day, not asked.
F-TR-007 confirms the Zurich calculator is used for every employee and G-05 confirms Zurich is the only source tax system, so canton-specific calculators are out of scope.
G-04 places transmission and change notifications in a separate requirement package, and F-TR-016 shows first-working-day changes as an example of that concern.
